subject: EdgeFin benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>, Priya Mishra <priya.mishra@edgefin.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeFin benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the performance / SLO qualification front so we can align on benchmark methodology.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary goal: validate model + infra configuration against EdgeFin latency SLOs under your expected workload shapes.
- Key SLOs discussed: 95th percentile latency target, first-byte (streaming) latency target, and sustained concurrency/throughput.
- Constraints: many requests are streaming (partial tokens returned), typical response sizes ~150-800 tokens depending on user flow.

What we need from EdgeFin to formalize the bench plan:
1) Confirm latency SLOs by response size (e.g., p95 <= 300ms for <= 256 tokens, p95 <= 600ms for 512 tokens, first-byte streaming <= 150ms) — we captured some numbers in the call but want them in writing.
2) Typical concurrency / throughput envelope (peak concurrent requests, sustained RPS or requests/min).
3) Representative prompt set (we discussed a 1k sample set to start + ability to share a larger 100k set for longer runs). JSONL or newline-delimited prompts preferred.
4) Any non-functional test constraints (IP allowlist for harness, redaction requirements, synthetic vs. production traces).

What Redwood will provide:
- Benchmark harness (attached: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip) with sprint instructions and reproducibility steps.
- Suggested prompt set template and a small reference prompt file to get started (attached: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- Measurement definitions: cold vs warm runs, warm-up iterations, how we measure p50/p95/p99 and streaming first-byte.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex/Priya: confirm the SLO numbers and concurrency envelope by EOD Monday (2026-06-08).
- EdgeFin to share sample prompt set (1k) and any privacy redaction guidance.
- Redwood SE (Marcus) to draft detailed benchmark methodology and schedule a 60-min smoke-test run (we can run on hosted or dedicated depending on your preference).

Attachments: edgefin-benchmark-requirements.xlsx (high-level targets), redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip (harness + runner).

If helpful I can also loop in our performance lead for a short technical sync.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>

Date: 2026-06-01T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up

Marissa — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side to make the methodology concrete: 

- Latency targets: our internal product team is looking for p95 <= 300ms for responses <= 256 tokens, and p95 <= 600ms for responses up to 512 tokens. For responses >512 tokens we are flexible but want p50/p95 visibility. We also care about first-byte for streaming: target is first-byte <= 150ms (user-perceived latency).
- Concurrency/throughput: typical peak concurrent requests today are ~60–80 concurrent active flows during market opens. Sustained throughput averages ~120 requests/min during business hours, spikes up to 350 requests/min for short bursts.
- Streaming: we use token streaming in 3 of our top flows (live estimates, alerts, and in-product chat). The harness should support chunked streaming and measuring first-byte + steady-state token rate.

We can provide a 1k anonymized prompt set by EOD Monday. We also have a larger 100k historical set our SRE team can provide if needed for longer runs.

A couple of asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the harness measures first-byte from TCP accept or from application-level first token emitted? For us, app-level first-token is the relevant metric.
2) For reproducibility, we need the exact seed and model variant pinned (model version, quantization, any kernel flags).

If you want, Marcus can run an initial warm-up run with our 1k set on your hosted environment to show baseline numbers.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, EdgeFin
alex.johnson@edgefin.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>, Priya Mishra <priya.mishra@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up

Thanks Alex — useful specifics. Below is a proposed benchmark methodology that aligns with your asks and with Redwood reproducibility requirements. Happy to iterate.

1) Measurement definitions
- First-byte latency (streaming): measure at application emit of first token (not TCP). We'll instrument the harness to mark t0 at request arrival and t_first_token at first token output. Report p50/p95/p99 for first-byte.
- Response latency: measure end-to-end time until final token emitted. Report p50/p95/p99 and mean.
- Throughput: measured as completed requests per second and tokens/second during steady-state.
- Warm vs cold: 3 cold runs (fresh process), then 5 warm runs; discard the cold-run data and report aggregated warm-run stats.

2) Workload shaping
- Use your 1k sample as the canonical prompt_set for initial smoke tests. For scale tests, use the 100k historical set. Provide a token-length distribution map (we can compute from your sample).
- Concurrency: run tests at target concurrencies [20, 40, 60, 80, 100] to map p95 curve. Include burst runs that ramp from 120 rps to 350 rps over 60s to simulate market opens.

3) Runtime configuration and reproducibility
- We'll pin model version (e.g., llamaX-13b-v1.2) and quantization profile in test metadata. The harness will output the exact runtime flags, kernel versions, and GPU driver details.
- We'll check for deterministic seeds for token sampling where applicable; for sampling-based endpoints we'll also run n=5 repeats and report variance.

4) Streaming specifics
- Harness will support chunked responses and report first-byte, median chunk interval, and effective token emission rate.

5) Artifacts and deliverables
- We will produce: raw run logs, aggregated percentiles, run-level metadata, and a reproducibility recipe (exact command line + environment).

6) Next steps
- EdgeFin: share the 1k anonymized prompt set (JSONL) and confirm where we can run the smoke test (hosted or dedicated). If hosted, we need an allowlist IP for the harness; if dedicated, we will coordinate access via your infra team.
- Redwood: schedule a 60-min smoke test window. I can run a warm-up + 3 warm runs and share results/plots.

Proposed windows (PST): 2026-06-08 09:00-10:30, 2026-06-09 14:00-15:30.

Quoting Alex's note on first-byte measurement for clarity:
> For reproducibility, we need the exact seed and model variant pinned (model version, quantization, any kernel flags).

We'll ensure the harness includes those fields in the run metadata.

\u0014Marcus
